summary: 失而复得的园艺笔记让人重新认识约翰斯顿如何营造希德科特花园，也为修复者判断哪些景观属于原设计提供了依据。
logic: 约翰斯顿建园与花园移交
接管后的修复如何改变花园
档案与失落的园艺笔记重现
借笔记重读园景与设计灵感

paragraphs.brief: 1949年，它只吸引了600名游客，在第一个公共赛季全程拿走了30英镑。
sentences: British gardens draw visitors from all over the world and in late July they are entering a second phase.
英国的花园吸引了来自世界各地的游客 7月底他们进入了第二阶段
As the roses are over, many private gardens have now had their open days, giving way to the public gardens of the English National Trust.
随着玫瑰花的结束，许多私人花园现已开放，让位于英国国家信托基金的公共花园。
Sixty years ago there was only one garden in the trust’s care, Hidcote Manor, near Chipping Campden in the Cotswolds.
六十年前，信托基金只有一个花园，即Cotswolds的Chipping Campden附近的Hidcote Manor。
In 1949 it attracted a mere 600 visitors and took all of £30 during its first public season.
1949年，它只吸引了600名游客，在第一个公共赛季全程拿走了30英镑。

paragraphs.brief: 如今，Hidcote作为设计和种植的杰作在全世界闻名。
sentences: Nowadays Hidcote is famous worldwide as a masterpiece of design and planting.
如今，Hidcote作为设计和种植的杰作在全世界闻名。
It is set to attract 150,000 visitors and raise nearly £1m from entrance tickets in this 60th anniversary year.
预计将吸引150,000名游客，并从入场票中筹集近100万英。

paragraphs.brief: 希德科特的花园是英国一个安静的美国人，害羞的劳伦斯·约翰斯顿少校的辉煌创造，他于1907年来到该地，与他丧偶的母亲格特鲁德·温思罗普(Gertrude Winthrop)一起生活。
sentences: Hidcote’s garden was the brilliant creation of a quiet American in Britain, the shy Major Lawrence Johnston, who arrived to live on the site in 1907 with his widowed mother, the twice-married Gertrude Winthrop.
希德科特的花园是英国一个安静的美国人，害羞的劳伦斯·约翰斯顿少校的辉煌创造，他于1907年来到该地，与他丧偶的母亲格特鲁德·温思罗普(Gertrude Winthrop)一起生活。
Mother Nature is seldom the only important mother behind a great garden.
大自然母亲很少是花园里唯一的重要母亲
By 1948 Winthrop was long dead but she continued to deny her son free access to the family capital, having tied £1m and more into trust so that he could enjoy only the income after her death.
到1948年，Winthrop早就去世了，但是她继续拒绝让儿子自由进入家庭资本，将100万英镑和更多的人置于信任之下，以便他只能在她死后享受收入。
She had seen and feared her son’s talent for expensive landscape gardening during their 17 years of adult life in Hidcote’s manor house.
她看到并担心她儿子在Hidcote庄园的17年成年生涯中拥有昂贵园艺的天赋。

paragraphs.brief: 暂时的，约翰斯顿同意，但即使是他的顾问也不确定他是否会运用他游荡的心态来解决这个问题。
sentences: By 1948 Johnston, ever unmarried, was in his late 70s and his mind was failing.
到1948年，约翰斯顿，曾经未婚，是在他70年代末期，他的头脑正在崩溃。
He was beset by the postwar menace of socialist taxes in Britain and was wanting to transfer his domicile to France, where he had made a second great garden at Serre de la Madone near Menton.
他受到英国社会主义税战后威胁的困扰，并想将他的住所转移到法国，在那里他在Menton附近的Serre de la Madone做了第二个伟大的花园。
The London society hostess Lady Sybil Colefax was encouraging him to solve his fiscal problems by giving Hidcote to the National Trust and then emigrating for most of the year.
伦敦社会主办人Sybil Colefax女士鼓励他解决财政问题，将Hidcote交给国家信托公司，然后在一年的大部分时间里移居国外。
Tentatively Johnston agreed but even his advisers were unsure if he would apply his wandering mind to the problem.
暂时的，约翰斯顿同意，但即使是他的顾问也不确定他是否会运用他游荡的心态来解决这个问题。

paragraphs.brief: James Lees -Milne 回忆起他日记里的紧张转移时刻：“国家信托局的非官方秘书。”
sentences: The National Trust’s unofficial secretary, James Lees-Milne, recalls the tense moment of transfer in his diaries.
James Lees -Milne 回忆起他日记里的紧张转移时刻：“国家信托局的非官方秘书。”
In a downstairs room at Hidcote the “conspirators”, Sybil Colefax and himself, held their breath as Johnston held the pen poised and a shadow crossed his face.
在Hidcote楼下的一间楼下房间里，“阴谋者”Sybil Colefax和他本人屏住呼吸，Johnston拿着笔，一个影子穿过他的脸。
They felt unable to rely on Johnston’s failing memory and so they told him that the crucial document before him was one of lesser importance.
他们觉得无法依赖约翰斯顿的失灵记忆，因此他们告诉他，他面前的关键文件不重要。
He signed and the trust acquired its first garden.
他签了字，信托人获得了它的第一个花园

paragraphs.brief: 20年前，约翰斯顿自己不得不让他的老妈妈被证明为精神无能。
sentences: Twenty years earlier Johnston himself had had to have his ageing mother certified as mentally incapable.
20年前，约翰斯顿自己不得不让他的老妈妈被证明为精神无能。
He had taken her to a rest clinic near Menton, where he began to buy the ground for his second superb garden, his alternative Hidcote in France.
他将她带到Menton附近的一家休息诊所，在那里他开始购买他的第二个超级花园的场地，即他在法国的替代花园Hidcote。
In 2002 I was shown an old sepia postcard-picture of his mother in the flower-decorated salon of this clinic, a touching record of their drama.
2002年，我看到他母亲的一张古老的Sepia明信片照片，出现在这个诊所的花饰沙龙，这是他们戏剧的感人记录。

paragraphs.brief: 令人惊讶的是，他们从未见过他的希德科特，直到他们的西辛赫斯特已经成熟；他们属于一个年轻的、后爱德华代的一代。
sentences: Having gained the garden, how on earth was the National Trust to cope with it?
有了花园国家信托基金怎么应付它呢？
We all forget how old Hidcote’s landscape already was.
我们都会忘记希德科特的风景已经多么古老。
Johnston had started to design it 40 years earlier in 1908 and had brought it to a peak in the early 1930s when he was already in his 60s.
Johnston在1908年40年前就开始设计了并在1930年代初达到了顶峰那时他已经60岁了
We think of him beside Harold Nicolson and Vita Sackville-West, creators of Sissinghurst, his garden’s only surviving equal.
我们想到他和哈罗德·尼科尔森和维塔·萨克维尔-西，希辛赫斯特的创造者，他的花园唯一的生存者。
Amazingly, they never saw his Hidcote until their Sissinghurst was already mature; and they belonged to a younger, post-Edwardian generation.
令人惊讶的是，他们从未见过他的希德科特，直到他们的西辛赫斯特已经成熟；他们属于一个年轻的、后爱德华代的一代。

paragraphs.brief: 到1948年，Hidcote的维修费用在战争期间因业主的权力失效而滑落。
sentences: By 1948 the maintenance at Hidcote had slipped during wartime as its owner’s powers failed.
到1948年，Hidcote的维修费用在战争期间因业主的权力失效而滑落。
Newly found photographs even show lines of cabbages being grown on the fabled Theatre Lawn as part of the war effort.
新发现的照片甚至显示，作为战争努力的一部分，在传说中的剧院草坪上种植了卷心菜。
Johnston had placed great faith in the skilled plantswoman Nancy Lindsay but she had many talents, including one for taking offence.
强斯顿对技术熟练的植物女郎南希·林赛深信不疑但她有很多天赋包括犯罪能力
A Garden Committee was ill-suited to dealing with her impassioned views and before long Lees-Milne believed that she had simply burned the crucial diaries and documents of the garden’s history.
花园委员会不适合处理她充满激情的观点。早在李斯-米勒内之前，她就认为她只是烧掉了花园历史的重要日记和文件。

paragraphs.brief: 到1955年，恢复希德科特的任务已经交给国家信托基金的新花园顾问，伟大的植物人格雷厄姆·托马斯。
sentences: By 1955 the task of reviving Hidcote had passed to the National Trust’s new gardens adviser, the great plantsman Graham Thomas.
到1955年，恢复希德科特的任务已经交给国家信托基金的新花园顾问，伟大的植物人格雷厄姆·托马斯。
Rare paeonies and half-hardy plants had been lost by the dozen as the trust had neither the staff nor the cash to preserve them.
由于信托基金既无工作人员也无现金保护这些植物，十几个人失去了稀有的植物和半硬的植物。
Thomas knew he had to rationalise and to extend the areas of public interest.
Thomas知道他必须合理化，扩大公共利益领域。
So he introduced new plants, new colours and a Mediterranean Bank where Johnston had had nothing of the sort.
所以他引进了新的植物，新的颜色以及一个地中海银行约翰斯顿没有这种东西
Hidcote survived to become an international icon because Thomas saved its superb structure of avenues, mixed hedges and evergreen rooms.
Hidcote幸存下来成为国际偶像，因为Thomas挽救了它的超级通道结构、混合树篱和常青房。
Johnston himself had referred to it as a “wild garden in a formal setting”, the most difficult legacy to maintain in style.
Johnston本人将它称为“正式环境中的荒凉花园”，这是保持风格的最困难的遗产。

paragraphs.brief: 自1949年以来，公众天真地仰慕托马斯的花卉，而不是少校的花卉。
sentences: Since 1949 the public has innocently been admiring Thomas’s flower-plantings, not the Major’s own.
自1949年以来，公众天真地仰慕托马斯的花卉，而不是少校的花卉。

paragraphs.brief: 托马斯和信任失去了他们并拉倒了房子。
sentences: The central red borders have become world famous but it was Thomas who added the emphasis on purple and dusky brown foliage.
中央红线已经成名但托马斯更强调紫色和紫色棕色叶子
When the important designer Russell Page visited Hidcote in 1934 he recorded borders of red and orange flowers and a matching haze of deep blue.
当重要的设计师罗素·佩吉 1934年访问希德科特时他记录了红花和橙花的边界以及一串相匹配的深蓝色烟雾
He also hailed the half-hardy plants in the summer house as a “gay museum”.
他还赞扬暑期之家的半硬植物是“同性恋博物馆”。
Thomas and the trust had lost them and pulled the house down.
托马斯和信任失去了他们并拉倒了房子。

paragraphs.brief: 我刚刚和目前的园丁Glyn Jones 坐在Hidcote的信托基金的小档案室里讨论了Hidcote过去的谜团
sentences: I have just sat in the trust’s small archive room at Hidcote with the present head gardener, Glyn Jones, and discussed the puzzles of Hidcote’s past.
我刚刚和目前的园丁Glyn Jones 坐在Hidcote的信托基金的小档案室里讨论了Hidcote过去的谜团
We talked of the memories of a former young gardener, Jack Percival, who only surfaced as a source in the 1990s.
我们谈到一位年轻的园丁杰克·佩西瓦尔的记忆，他直到1990年代才露面。
Invaluably he remembered constructing Johnston’s lost rock garden with truckloads of sawdust and chippings and a stream below them to simulate the snow-melt in Alpine mountains.
他记不起建造约翰斯顿失落的岩石花园装满了木屑和碎屑以及下面的一条溪流以模拟阿尔卑斯山的雪熔
The site has now been re-excavated and pools and water-basins have been rediscovered exactly as Percival had remembered after 60 years.
现已重新挖掘了该地，并重新发现了水池和水盆，这与Percival60年后所记得的完全一样。

paragraphs.brief: 琼斯然后让我震惊地问我是否想看“旧日记和笔记本”。
sentences: At the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, lists have also been found of plants from foreign collections which were sent to Hidcote across 20 years.
在皇家植物园爱丁堡也发现了外国收藏的植物 20年来被送到希德科特
They help to focus our ideas of the amazing range which Hidcote once tested and held.
它们帮助我们集中思考希德科特曾经测试过并且坚持过的惊人范围。
Jones then brought me up in shock by asking if I would like to see the “old diaries and notebooks”.
琼斯然后让我震惊地问我是否想看“旧日记和笔记本”。
Diaries?
日记？
Notebooks?
笔记本？
They were all supposed to have been burned or lost.
他们本该被烧掉或丢失的

paragraphs.brief: 里面没有信件，只有约翰斯顿1929年和1932年的个人日记，还有1925年至1928年的一本类似的书，有他的素描和笔记。
sentences: Out of a padded envelope from a locked drawer the head gardener produced three hardly believable survivors: little hard-backed blue notebooks and daybooks.
园丁从一个锁着的抽屉里拿出了一个封装信封产生了三个难以相信的幸存者：很少硬背的蓝色笔记本和日记本
In 2002 Jones had started to give talks about Hidcote’s lost early history and to appeal for memories from his audience.
2002年，琼斯开始谈论Hidcote丧失的早期历史，并呼吁他的听众记住过去。
A few months later an envelope arrived for him, postmarked in Somerset.
几个月后，一个信封寄到萨默塞特，贴上邮戳。
There was no letter inside, only Johnston’s personal daybooks for 1929 and 1932 and a similar book of his sketches and notes between 1925 and 1928.
里面没有信件，只有约翰斯顿1929年和1932年的个人日记，还有1925年至1928年的一本类似的书，有他的素描和笔记。

paragraphs.brief: 我一看一页一页的铅笔观察和草图，就握手颤抖。这个设计花园的神秘天才，几乎没有任何人能靠自己活下来。
sentences: Whoever had hung on to them so long and quietly turned them in?
谁一直坚持着他们悄悄地把他们交出来？
My hands shook as I looked at page after page of pencil-observations and sketches by the enigmatic genius of garden design, a man from whom almost nothing else has survived in his own hand.
我一看一页一页的铅笔观察和草图，就握手颤抖。这个设计花园的神秘天才，几乎没有任何人能靠自己活下来。
They do not contain revelations about a private life or longings.
它们不包含关于私生活或渴望的迹象。
They are far more interesting.
它们更有趣。
They are classic records of “house and home”.
它们是典型的“房屋和住宅”记录。

paragraphs.brief: Johnston在一页后写道，植物在他脑海中，与当天的客人一起吃午饭或玩他最爱的网球，有用手工艺者的地址，以及从睡梦中吸水到毒虫和老鼠的食谱。
sentences: On page after page Johnston has noted down the plants in his mind, interspersed with the day’s guests for lunch or for a game of his beloved tennis, the addresses of useful craftsmen and recipes for anything from sleeping draughts to poisons for slugs and rats.
Johnston在一页后写道，植物在他脑海中，与当天的客人一起吃午饭或玩他最爱的网球，有用手工艺者的地址，以及从睡梦中吸水到毒虫和老鼠的食谱。
The novelist Edith Wharton is noted for lunch and overnight visits and then there are lists of menders of broken china or sources of antique furniture in Paris or trousers in Warwick.
小说家伊迪丝·沃顿在午餐和过夜访问时被注意到，然后有巴黎破碎瓷器或古董家具来源或华威克裤子的清单。
Above all there are the plants, densest in springtime, in years when Hidcote was at its height.
最重要的是那些植物，春天最稠密，在Hidcote处于它的高度的年份。
Ceaselessly the Major’s pencil was listing scores of plants whose names I have never read before.
少校手中的铅笔不停地记下一种又一种植物的名字，许多名字我以前从未见过。
Here are his notes for this very day, 80 years ago: “Wulfenia amherstiana, Kew.
80年前的今天，他的笔记如下：“Wulfenia Amherstiana，Kew。
Lavatera.
岩浆。
Agie to tea.
来杯茶吧
Rose Penelope.
萝丝·佩内洛普
Linaria macedonica.
莱娜莉娅·曼塞多尼卡
Halesia carolina monticola [the Snowdrop Tree, of which his plant later won a Royal Horticultural Society Award].
Halesia Carolina Monticola[雪滴树，他的植物后来获得皇家园艺学会奖]。
Godetia Mauve Queen.
戈黛蒂娅·莫芙·奎恩
Omphalodes linifolia,” the latter being a lovely annual which we should scatter more often in the front of flowerbeds.
” 后者是一个可爱的一年，我们应该在花床前更经常地散开。
How many of you garden-readers will have noted a fraction as much by teatime today?
今天茶时，你们这些看花园的人会注意到多少分数？

paragraphs.brief: 发现这些笔记本给希德科特带来了机会和挑战
sentences: The discovery of the notebooks has offered Hidcote a chance and a challenge.
发现这些笔记本给希德科特带来了机会和挑战
Inspired by them, an anonymous American has given the garden £1.6m, to be matched by the trust (£1.2m of the necessary pledge has already been raised).
在他们的启发下，一个匿名美国人给了花园160万英镑，与信托相匹配(已经筹集了120万英镑的必要认捐)。
Crucial work on paths, the famous pool and the drains has been carried out and the old summer house has been replicated together with the former house for sheltering rare alpines.
道路、著名游泳池和排水沟方面的重要工作已经完成，旧的夏令营与前高山避难所一起复制。
They might surprise visitors but they are Johnston’s ideas restored.
他们可能会给访客带来惊喜... ...但他们是强斯顿的主意得到恢复的
Now the trust must take its collection of plants up one more notch, as we know the very things which appealed to the Major in the garden’s golden years.
现在，信任必须把收藏的植物再加一点，因为我们知道花园黄金年代里吸引少校的东西。
The challenge should be thrilling.
挑战应该是令人兴奋的。

paragraphs.brief: 但这不是很久以前的事吗？" 一个非园艺学者在耐心地听到我的兴奋之后问我。
sentences: It has certainly thrilled me.
我当然很兴奋
“But isn’t it all so long ago?” a non-gardening academic asked me after patiently hearing my excitement out.
但这不是很久以前的事吗？" 一个非园艺学者在耐心地听到我的兴奋之后问我。
On the contrary it is still with us, especially on evenings as heavenly as those we had recently.
相反，它仍然与我们同在，特别是在我们最近所经历的天堂般的夜晚。
I walked up the greatest central vista in British gardening, the design I regard as the greatest in British art in the past century.
我走过英国园艺界最伟大的中心，设计我认为是过去一个世纪中英国艺术界最伟大的。
It was the work of an American genius, building an un-American garden of his own.
这是一位美国天才的作品，建造了一个非美国的花园。

It passes between the red borders, where I now want to root out the brown leaves and purple hazels and even restore the Major’s ornamental grasses and the pampas grasses which photos show to have stood there instead.
它穿过红线，我现在想根除棕色叶子和紫色子，甚至恢复少校的装饰草和照片显示站在那里的Pampas草。

paragraphs.brief: 我爬过双眼双眼的好步子顶尖的屋顶无法追溯到任何一处无论是荷兰人还是英语
sentences: I climb the fine steps past the twin gazebos with pointed roofs which are not to be traced to any one source, neither Dutch nor English.
我爬过双眼双眼的好步子顶尖的屋顶无法追溯到任何一处无论是荷兰人还是英语
On either side of the steps I bless Thomas for the velvet-red Clematis Royal Velours.
在两边的阶梯上我祝福托马斯给天鹅绒红的克莱马提斯·罗亚尔·维卢尔斯
I then walk on between the double blocks of clipped hornbeams edging the upper terrace, whose proportional relation to the avenue convinces me that the inspiration came from France.
我走在双层角束之间夹着上方阳台与街道的成比例关系使我相信灵感来自法国

paragraphs.brief: 时下流行一种猜测，认为少校受到了英国托马斯·莫森关于当代设计的书籍影响。我不认同这种说法，在我看来，莫森的才智平庸得多。
sentences: I do not believe the fashionable guess nowadays that the Major was influenced by books on contemporary design by Britain’s Thomas Mawson, an altogether commoner mind.
时下流行一种猜测，认为少校受到了英国托马斯·莫森关于当代设计的书籍影响。我不认同这种说法，在我看来，莫森的才智平庸得多。
Beyond their bare trunks run the beds in which Johnston planted heavenly blues and anchusas.
在他们裸体的箱子外运行床强斯顿种植天堂蓝调和安楚萨斯。
Then, two elegant brick pillars hold portrait-busts as if in Italy, reminding us how Johnston had travelled widely in Europe as Mawson had not.
然后，两块优雅的砖柱像在意大利一样摆放着肖像碎片，提醒我们约翰斯顿在欧洲是如何象莫森没有那样走得非常远的。

paragraphs.brief: 在他们之间，两个细细的铁门似乎从通道的脚进入了上方天堂。
sentences: Between them two fine gates of pierced iron seem from the foot of the avenue to be giving entry into heaven above.
在他们之间，两个细细的铁门似乎从通道的脚进入了上方天堂。
Will the garden-angels let me in?
花园天使会让我进去吗？

paragraphs.brief: 我记得约翰斯顿自己改信天主教，在法国我如何看到他的毕生祷告书，书上写着笔记本和笔记本一样的笔记本，并被他的土生土长的园艺手在书页上沾上。
sentences: I remember Johnston’s own conversion to Catholicism and how in France I have seen his lifelong prayerbook, marked with the same pencil script as his notebooks and stained on its pages by his earthy gardening hands.
我记得约翰斯顿自己改信天主教，在法国我如何看到他的毕生祷告书，书上写着笔记本和笔记本一样的笔记本，并被他的土生土长的园艺手在书页上沾上。

Only when you pass through the gates do you see that they give on to earthly paradise instead: grass fields, old evergreen oaks, sheep beyond the hidden ha-ha and, further still, a view across what Henry James once described as the “pastoral genius of England”.
只有当你穿过大门时，你才看到他们把东西给了地球的天堂：草地、古老的绿橡树、隐藏的公顷以外的绵羊，还有亨利·詹姆斯曾经称之为“英格兰的牧业天才”的景象。

paragraphs.brief: 那天晚上，当我读约翰斯顿长期丢失的笔记本时，这个天堂的景色被亮着的金光照亮。
sentences: On the evening when I read Johnston’s long-lost notebooks the view across this heaven was lit with a golden light.
那天晚上，当我读约翰斯顿长期丢失的笔记本时，这个天堂的景色被亮着的金光照亮。
It was as if their faithful author was approving in spirit that his life’s masterpiece could give such joy and still be understood.
他们的忠实作者似乎在精神上赞同他的杰作，他的生活能够带来如此的欢乐，并且仍然可以被理解。

points: 失而复得的园艺笔记让人重新认识约翰斯顿如何营造希德科特花园，也为修复者判断哪些景观属于原设计提供了依据。
园主与花园的创建 → 移交后的修复 → 档案与笔记重现 → 用记录重读设计
clauses: Tentatively Johnston agreed but even his advisers were unsure ….
连接词 if 引出“if he would apply his wandering mind to the problem”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
They felt unable to rely on Johnston’s failing memory and so they told him ….
“that the crucial document before him was one of lesser importance”补足 told 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 told 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
lead: Robin Lane Fox writes about the American genius behind a remarkable garden in the Cotswolds.
罗宾·莱恩·福克斯介绍了英国科茨沃尔德一座名园背后的美国园艺家。
